claims.text: The as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 baseline has a quasi-static yield strength of about 786 MPa, compressive strength of about 1314 MPa, and fracture strain of about 13.5%.
A temperature of 1000–1200 K corresponds to approximately 0.7–0.8 Tm for HfZrTiTa0.53.
Multi-pass hot forging at 1000–1200 K with 10–30% strain per pass, followed by annealing at 600–800 K for 0.5–1 hour, will create a heterogeneous grain-size distribution in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed processing will produce coarse grains interspersed with fine, partially recrystallized regions.
The low-temperature anneal will stabilize the fine recrystallized regions.
Heterogeneous coarse and fine grain regions will promote dislocation storage and internal back-stress.
Dislocation accumulation and internal back-stress will enhance strain hardening.
The heterogeneous microstructure will delay shear-band nucleation and adiabatic shear localization during rapid deformation.
Adiabatic shear bands can develop during dynamic compression through competition between strain-rate hardening and heat softening.
The processed alloy will retain similar or slightly higher yield and compressive strengths than the as-cast alloy.
The processed alloy will exhibit significantly improved strain hardening relative to the as-cast baseline.
The processed alloy will have higher uniform deformability, represented by fracture strain exceeding 13.5%.
The processed alloy will resist adiabatic shear-band formation better than the as-cast baseline.
The processed alloy will absorb more impact-induced energy than the as-cast baseline.
The predicted improvements apply from approximately 10^-3 s^-1 through 10^3 s^-1 under quasi-static and dynamic compression.
The effects may differ under substantially non-adiabatic conditions or at strain rates far above 10^3 s^-1.
